paragraphs: This paper asks whether a reinforcement learning algorithm can keep its total regret finite even while interacting over infinitely many episodes. Regret measures the accumulated cost of choosing actions that fall short of optimal behavior. The authors study environments whose rewards and transitions are approximately linear in a feature representation, allowing a bounded amount of modeling error.

Their algorithm, Cert-LSVI-UCB, uses a certified estimator to support a detailed analysis of regression across multiple learning phases. Its guarantee depends on the minimum suboptimality gap, which separates optimal choices from inferior ones. The modeling error must be sufficiently small relative to that gap, the feature dimension, and the planning horizon.

Under the stated condition, cumulative regret is bounded with high probability by approximately d³H⁵/Δ, suppressing logarithmic factors. Crucially, the bound does not grow with the number of episodes. This is a conditional, instance-dependent guarantee: the result supports finite total regret under controlled misspecification, without requiring assumptions about a prior distribution.
neurips-2024-achieving-constant-regret-i.tldr: Cert-LSVI-UCB achieves episode-independent regret with high probability when linear approximation error is sufficiently small relative to the suboptimality gap.

paragraphs: Training neural networks on embedded devices creates a different resource problem from simply running them. Backpropagation needs stored activation maps, and those intermediate representations can consume substantial memory. This paper targets that storage requirement as a major obstacle to bringing learning onto devices with tight computational and memory budgets.

The authors investigate two ways to compress activation maps: Singular Value Decomposition and its tensor counterpart, High-Order Singular Value Decomposition. Both replace the stored representation with a smaller decomposition intended to retain the features that matter for learning. Comparing the two connects the structure of the compressed representation to the practical memory demands of training.

The paper reports considerable memory savings while preserving learning-relevant information, together with theoretical convergence guarantees. Experiments across mainstream architectures and tasks show a superior tradeoff between generalization and memory footprint relative to the compared methods. The contribution therefore concerns training efficiency: activation storage can be reduced while maintaining a favorable balance between resource use and learned performance.
neurips-2024-activation-map-compression-.tldr: Compressing stored activations with matrix and tensor decompositions improves the tradeoff between training memory and generalization.

paragraphs: Recommendation data can be biased because the factors influencing what users select also influence their feedback. Correcting for recorded features is insufficient when relevant factors remain hidden. Existing approaches described in the paper either assume substantial knowledge about the strength of this hidden confounding or use costly randomized trial data to calibrate a model.

MetaDebias instead uses a mixture of observational datasets, assuming that some are affected by hidden confounding and others are not. The motivating case involves users with incomplete personal information alongside users with complete information. This distinction is an assumption of the setup: the latter group is treated as providing data without hidden confounding.

The method uses meta-learning and a two-level optimization procedure to jointly model oracle error imputation and bias from hidden confounding. Experiments on three public datasets report state-of-the-art performance under hidden confounding, both with and without randomized trial data. The findings support heterogeneous observational data as a useful resource for debiasing when the proposed mixture assumption applies.
neurips-2024-addressing-hidden-confoundi.tldr: MetaDebias uses observational datasets with differing confounding conditions to improve recommendation learning, with or without randomized trial data.

paragraphs: Language-model agents often retrieve stored experiences or external knowledge before planning and acting. AgentPoison examines how this dependence can become a vulnerability when the retrieved material is unverified. Its attack targets the agent's long-term memory or retrieval knowledge base, rather than requiring changes to the underlying language model.

The method optimizes a backdoor trigger so that instructions containing it are likely to retrieve malicious demonstrations. Instructions without the trigger are intended to retain normal behavior. This makes the retrieval process central to the attack: a small amount of poisoned material can influence which examples the agent uses to guide its actions, without additional model training or fine-tuning.

Experiments cover autonomous driving, knowledge-intensive question answering, and a healthcare agent. For each agent, the authors report average attack success of at least 80%, benign-performance impact of at most 1%, and a poisoning rate below 0.1%. These results demonstrate a targeted retrieval vulnerability across the tested agents, including cases where ordinary performance remains largely unchanged.
neurips-2024-agentpoison-red-teaming-llm.tldr: AgentPoison shows that small amounts of poisoned retrieval content can trigger harmful agent behavior while leaving ordinary performance largely intact.

paragraphs: Graph classifiers may need to learn new classes from only a few labeled nodes while retaining knowledge of earlier classes. The paper identifies two problems with existing approaches: constructing memories can require many samples, and extensive adjustment of the graph neural network can erase past knowledge. Mecoin addresses memory construction and knowledge preservation together.

A Structured Memory Unit stores class prototypes, which act as compact representations of previously seen classes. The Memory Construction module updates new prototypes through interactions between nodes and the stored prototypes. A separate adaptive module distinguishes prototype learning from class-representation learning, while a knowledge interchange module feeds past knowledge back into the graph neural network.

This separation aims to reduce reliance on heavy parameter fine-tuning while keeping old class information available. The authors analyze generalization error and examine how different distillation methods affect performance, including discussion through VC-dimension. Their comparisons report higher classification accuracy and lower forgetting rates than related methods, supporting the proposed memory organization for incremental graph learning with scarce labels.
neurips-2024-an-efficient-memory-module-.tldr: Mecoin organizes class prototypes and transfers stored knowledge to improve few-shot graph learning while reducing forgetting.

paragraphs: Deep neural collapse describes the unusually rigid organization of representations found in the final layers of trained networks. Many explanations treat those representations without explicitly incorporating the training data. This paper develops a data-dependent mechanism based on the average gradient outer product, or AGOP, which summarizes input-output gradient structure across the training set.

The authors study Deep Recursive Feature Machines, which repeatedly transform data using the AGOP and then apply an untrained random feature map. They show both theoretically and empirically that neural collapse arises in these models from the AGOP projection at each layer. This supplies a concrete feature-learning process through which the observed representation structure can emerge.

The paper also presents evidence that the mechanism extends to neural networks more broadly. In networks trained in the feature-learning regime, weight singular vectors and singular values can account for most of the collapse in variation within classes. Their strong relationship with AGOP structure supports the proposed explanation, while the broader-network claim remains evidence-based rather than a universal theorem.
neurips-2024-average-gradient-outer-prod.tldr: The paper establishes an AGOP-based mechanism for neural collapse in Deep Recursive Feature Machines and finds supporting evidence in broader neural networks.

paragraphs: B'MOJO addresses how a sequence model can combine explicit retention of past information with a compressed memory that fades over time. Transformer context and state-space models emphasize different forms of memory. The proposed architecture makes them adjustable within one composable module, while allowing memory to grow to a finite size that need not be specified beforehand.

Drawing on Stochastic Realization Theory, the framework accommodates short-term context, learned weights, recurrent state, and long-term storage with asynchronous retrieval. The authors show that Transformers, Mamba, and Jamba fit within the framework as special cases. They also describe an implementation designed to stack and scale efficiently on hardware.

In associative recall and related tasks, B'MOJO outperforms the tested state-space and hybrid models. Language modeling reaches comparable perplexity to similarly sized models up to 1.4 billion parameters, with training up to 10% faster. Models trained on sequences up to 8,000 tokens also show better inference on longer sequences tested up to 32,000 tokens, supporting the value of adjustable memory.
neurips-2024-b-mojo-hybrid-state-space-r.tldr: B'MOJO combines explicit and fading memory, improving tested recall and longer-sequence inference while maintaining competitive language modeling.

paragraphs: Solving a partial differential equation often requires information about the system that measurements do not fully provide. Missing observations or unknown coefficients can prevent direct use of classical solvers and weaken existing learned approaches. DiffusionPDE focuses on this incomplete-information setting, treating reconstruction of the missing quantities as part of the solving problem.

The method uses a generative diffusion model to learn the joint distribution of equation solutions and coefficients. Modeling them together provides a learned prior over how these quantities relate. The framework can then fill in missing information while solving the equation, rather than requiring a complete description of the system before the process begins.

The authors report accurate results across a broad range of PDEs under partial observation, with significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods in both forward and inverse problems. The stated contribution is a common generative framework for these two directions. Its findings support learning relationships between solutions and coefficients as a useful way to handle incomplete measurements.
neurips-2024-diffusionpde-generative-pde.tldr: DiffusionPDE jointly models solutions and coefficients to solve PDEs while reconstructing information missing from observations.

paragraphs: EpiCare provides a benchmark for reinforcement learning methods that choose treatments over a patient's course of care. It is designed to reflect difficulties associated with longitudinal healthcare, including limited data, short treatment episodes, sparse rewards, incomplete observations, and variation in treatment effects. These features make both learning and evaluating treatment strategies challenging.

The authors test five offline reinforcement learning models and five off-policy evaluation techniques. Offline learning uses existing experience to develop a policy, while off-policy evaluation assesses a policy using data collected under other behavior. Examining both is important because a promising treatment policy also needs a credible estimate of how it would perform.

The results suggest that offline learning may improve on existing care standards when large datasets are available, but that this promise does not appear to carry over to the benchmark's moderate and low data settings. Several commonly used evaluation techniques also perform inadequately. These findings raise concerns about meaningful policy assessment in this benchmark and motivate better methods for medical reinforcement learning.
neurips-2024-epicare-a-reinforcement-lea.tldr: EpiCare exposes weaknesses in offline treatment-policy learning and evaluation, particularly when available data is limited.

paragraphs: Forecasting several time series together requires deciding which channels should share information. Treating each channel separately can miss useful interactions and generalize poorly to unseen instances. Mixing every channel can introduce irrelevant information and oversmooth the representations. This paper seeks a way to preserve useful relationships without indiscriminately combining all channels.

The authors observe a connection between similarity within a pair of channels and the performance benefit obtained from mixing them. Their Channel Clustering Module dynamically groups channels according to intrinsic similarities. It then uses information about those groups instead of relying on individual channel identities, providing a shared organization for related signals.

Experiments on real-world datasets report average improvements of 2.4% for long-term forecasting and 7.2% for short-term forecasting when enhancing channel-independent and channel-dependent models. The module also enables zero-shot forecasting with mainstream forecasting models. Its clusters reveal patterns shared across channels, offering interpretability alongside the measured forecasting improvements and a more selective approach to information sharing.
neurips-2024-from-similarity-to-superior.tldr: Dynamically clustering similar time-series channels improves forecasting and enables information sharing based on relationships rather than channel identity.

paragraphs: Personalized image generators often assume that the concepts a user wants to generate remain fixed. This paper instead considers a sequence of customization tasks in which new concepts arrive over time. Learning those additions can make a model forget earlier concepts or neglect them when composing images, creating two related obstacles to continued customization.

The proposed Concept-Incremental text-to-image Diffusion Model addresses forgetting with a concept consolidation loss and elastic weight aggregation. These components distinguish knowledge specific to a task from knowledge shared across tasks. During inference, the method combines low-rank weights associated with earlier concepts according to their contributions, keeping previously learned customization knowledge involved in generation.

To address concept neglect, the model also uses a synthesis strategy that controls image context according to user conditions. It draws on region features and noise estimation to guide that control. Experiments report improvements over existing custom diffusion models. The contribution combines preservation of old concepts with control over how concepts appear, supporting customization that can evolve across successive learning tasks.
neurips-2024-how-to-continually-adapt-te.tldr: CIDM combines concept-preserving learning and context-controlled synthesis to support successive image customization tasks.

paragraphs: This paper studies how a participant can learn to bid across repeated auctions involving multiple units sold at a uniform price. Electricity producers participating in day-ahead markets motivate the setting. Opposing bids are treated as adversarial, so the learning problem does not rely on a favorable statistical model of other participants' behavior.

The central contribution is a new representation of the bid space that lets an algorithm exploit the auction's structure. Under bandit feedback, the regret bound improves from approximately K^(7/4)T^(3/4) to K^(4/3)T^(2/3), with logarithmic factors suppressed. The authors state that the improved rate is tight up to logarithmic terms, giving a theoretical characterization of achievable learning performance.

The paper also considers feedback that reveals every winning bid, motivated by electricity reserve markets. Depending on the auction outcome, this supplies an intermediate amount of information between bandit and full-information feedback. For that setting, the proposed algorithm has regret approximately K^(5/2)√T. The results connect better learning guarantees to both bid-space structure and the information revealed after an auction.
neurips-2024-improved-learning-rates-in-.tldr: A new bid-space model improves regret guarantees for repeated uniform-price auctions, with stronger rates when winning bids are revealed.

paragraphs: Reasoning from documents requires recognizing how the supplied facts connect before using them to reach an answer. This paper argues that efforts focused mainly on the reasoning process can overlook that preliminary task. If the model interacts only superficially with the context, useful logical relationships may remain unclear and redundant material may interfere.

InfoRE introduces an explicit information-reorganization stage before reasoning. It first extracts logical relationships from contextual material such as paragraphs or documents, then removes redundant content. The model reasons over this reorganized information. The approach therefore changes the material presented to the reasoning stage, making connections clearer while reducing potential sources of noise.

The authors evaluate InfoRE with Llama2-70B, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 on several tasks requiring multiple reasoning steps over contextual information. In a zero-shot setting, they report an average absolute improvement of 4% across tasks. These results support preparing the context as a useful component of reasoning performance, alongside improvements to the subsequent process of deriving an answer.
neurips-2024-information-re-organization.tldr: InfoRE improves contextual reasoning by extracting logical relationships and removing redundant information before the model reasons.

paragraphs: Local Bayesian optimization searches for good inputs to a black-box function by using a surrogate model near the current search region. Some methods approximate gradients and take steps resembling gradient descent. This paper asks whether those steps make sufficient use of the distributional information supplied by a Gaussian process surrogate.

The authors relate gradient descent steps to steps that minimize an upper confidence bound, or UCB. They show that minimizing this bound can provide a better local strategy when the surrogate is a Gaussian process. Their MinUCB algorithm replaces the gradient descent step in GIBO with UCB minimization, incorporating the surrogate's upper-bound information into the choice of where to move.

The analysis establishes a convergence rate similar to GIBO's. A further look-ahead modification produces LA-MinUCB, described as a more efficient algorithm. Experiments on synthetic and real-world functions support the effectiveness of both approaches. The finding is that upper-bound-guided movement can improve local search; the paper does not claim it universally dominates every gradient-based strategy.
neurips-2024-minimizing-ucb-a-better-loc.tldr: MinUCB improves local Bayesian search by minimizing a Gaussian process upper confidence bound while retaining a comparable convergence rate.

paragraphs: Representing motion with discrete codes can be useful for generation, but quantization introduces approximation error. Earlier approaches commonly compress an entire body pose into a single code. MoGenTS changes the unit of representation to an individual joint, reducing how much information each vector must encode while retaining relationships among joints.

The resulting representation is a two-dimensional token map organized around joints and time. This structure preserves both spatial relationships within the body and temporal movement patterns. The authors build a framework around it using a joint-level vector-quantized autoencoder, a two-dimensional masking technique, and attention designed to capture spatial and temporal signals together.

This design makes operations associated with two-dimensional images available for motion modeling while keeping the representation tied to motion's joint-and-time structure. Experiments report significant improvements across datasets, including FID reductions of 26.6% on HumanML3D and 29.9% on KIT-ML. The results support joint-level quantization and explicit spatial-temporal modeling as an effective combination for improving generated motion.
neurips-2024-mogents-motion-generation-b.tldr: MoGenTS represents individual joints as a two-dimensional motion token map and improves generation through spatial-temporal modeling.

paragraphs: Language models can become outdated as new documents accumulate, but repeatedly adapting a large parameter set is expensive. Memory of Amortized Contexts, or MAC, approaches updating through a memory bank. New documents are compressed into compact modulations that store useful information and can later influence the model's answers.

The system learns an encoder through amortization-based meta-learning. Once learned, the encoder replaces an otherwise required optimization procedure with a single forward pass. At question-answering time, MAC selects relevant stored document information and combines it into one question-conditioned modulation. This adapts the behavior of a frozen language model without requiring additional gradient updates at test time.

The memory bank separates accumulating new information from repeatedly changing the language model's weights. Experiments report advantages in online adaptation performance, time efficiency, and memory efficiency, alongside strong knowledge retention. The authors also show that MAC can be combined with retrieval-augmented generation and improve its performance, making the memory mechanism useful alongside that existing approach to supplying external knowledge.
neurips-2024-online-adaptation-of-langua.tldr: MAC compresses new documents into reusable memory modulations that adapt a frozen language model without test-time gradient updates.

paragraphs: Posterior sampling is a way to make decisions while accounting for uncertainty in contextual bandit problems. A Gaussian prior makes this computation convenient, but limits the kinds of initial distributions the model can express. This paper investigates whether a diffusion-model prior can provide richer distributions while retaining practical sampling procedures.

The proposed algorithms break posterior sampling into a chain of approximate conditional distributions, one for each stage of reverse diffusion. Each conditional distribution is obtained using a Laplace approximation. This turns the richer diffusion prior into a sequence of locally manageable approximation steps, borrowing the simplicity and efficiency associated with Gaussian-prior methods.

The authors establish asymptotic consistency for their approximations and report good empirical performance across several contextual bandit problems. Asymptotic consistency describes their limiting behavior; the algorithms are still approximate posterior samplers. The contribution is a way to combine expressive prior modeling with tractable online decision-making, supported by both a theoretical property and experiments in the stated bandit setting.
neurips-2024-online-posterior-sampling-w.tldr: The paper uses successive Laplace approximations to make posterior sampling with expressive diffusion priors practical for contextual bandits.

paragraphs: In-context learning lets a language model respond to a new task using examples in its prompt, without updating its parameters. This paper studies that behavior through binary classification decision boundaries: the dividing regions where the model switches from predicting one class to the other. These boundaries make aspects of the model's learned behavior visible.

The authors find that current language models often produce irregular, nonsmooth boundaries on simple classification tasks, including linear ones. This observation reveals behavior that a single accuracy score may not describe: the model's classification rule can have an uneven shape even when the task admits a simple relationship between inputs and labels.

The study investigates factors affecting these boundaries and ways to improve their generalization. It assesses methods with and without fine-tuning, architectural differences, and active prompting techniques intended to smooth boundaries using data efficiently. The findings offer a way to inspect in-context learning and provide practical improvements for robustness and generalizability, with the reported irregularity framed as a frequent observation rather than a universal property.
neurips-2024-probing-the-decision-bounda.tldr: Decision-boundary probes reveal frequent irregularities in in-context classification and help investigate methods for improving its generalization.

paragraphs: A degraded image already contains useful low-frequency information about the image to be restored. Conventional diffusion restoration methods condition generation on that image but still begin from Gaussian white noise. Resfusion changes the diffusion process so restoration can start directly from a noisy version of the degraded image, using information already present.

The framework introduces a residual term into forward diffusion and trains the model to predict a weighted combination of residual and noise, called resnoise. The authors specify the quantitative relationship between its components. A smooth equivalence transformation determines an acceleration step while preserving existing noise schedules and keeping training and inference aligned.

Although its starting point changes, the inference process retains the DDPM form. Experiments report competitive restoration performance on ISTD, LOL, and Raindrop using only five sampling steps. The paper also describes applying the framework to image generation. Its central finding is that incorporating the degraded image into the diffusion construction can support effective restoration with a short sampling process.
neurips-2024-resfusion-denoising-diffusi.tldr: Resfusion incorporates residual information into diffusion and achieves competitive image restoration with five sampling steps.

paragraphs: A model of human vision can match overall accuracy while missing how long people take to decide. RTify focuses on this temporal aspect of behavior. It learns to align the evolving computation of a recurrent neural network with human reaction times, connecting the duration of model processing to the timing of perceptual choices.

The framework introduces an approximation that allows human reaction times to constrain how many recurrent steps a model uses to solve a task. The authors evaluate the approach across psychophysics experiments. They also use it to optimize an ideal-observer network for a speed-accuracy tradeoff without human data; the resulting model accounts well for human reaction-time measurements.

A further application trains a deep learning version of the Wong-Wang decision-making model and combines it with a convolutional model of visual processing. Evaluation includes artificial and natural images. Together, these studies support reaction time as a useful target for aligning vision models with human behavior and connecting visual processing to decision dynamics.
neurips-2024-rtify-aligning-deep-neural-.tldr: RTify links recurrent computation to reaction times to better model the timing and accuracy of human perceptual decisions.

paragraphs: Combinatorial problems require choosing among arrangements or combinations and play important roles in logistics and resource management. This paper examines language models as tools for these difficult optimization tasks. It introduces Self-Guiding Exploration, a prompting strategy that organizes exploration, task decomposition, and refinement into a single process.

For each problem, SGE generates several reasoning trajectories rather than following only one proposed route. It breaks those trajectories into actionable subtasks, carries them out sequentially, and refines the resulting solutions. The approach aims to use the model's own exploration to guide subsequent work, connecting alternative plans with concrete steps and opportunities to improve the outcome.

The authors report an improvement exceeding 27.84% in combinatorial optimization performance over existing prompting strategies. They also report accuracy 2.46% higher than the best existing results on other reasoning tasks spanning arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning. These are empirical performance findings: they support the usefulness of the prompting procedure across the tested tasks without establishing a general guarantee of globally optimal solutions.
neurips-2024-self-guiding-exploration-fo.tldr: Self-Guiding Exploration combines multiple reasoning paths, sequential subtasks, and refinement to improve tested combinatorial optimization performance.

paragraphs: Shapley values assign contributions to individual entities, such as input features or training examples. Shapley interactions extend that idea to groups, helping explain joint contributions that individual attributions do not capture. Computing these quantities has exponential complexity, making efficient algorithms and meaningful comparisons important for practical use.

The shapiq package brings algorithms for Shapley values and interactions of any order into a common Python framework. It is designed to work across applications and incorporates methods that use structural assumptions or probabilistic estimates to manage computation. The package also supports explaining and visualizing feature interactions in predictions from several kinds of machine learning models.

A benchmarking suite covers 11 machine learning applications and supplies precomputed games with ground-truth values. This gives researchers a shared basis for assessing computational performance across domains. Supported explanation settings include vision transformers, language models, and tree models through TreeSHAP-IQ. The contribution combines usable explanation tools with evaluation infrastructure, making group-level attribution methods easier to apply and study systematically.
neurips-2024-shapiq-shapley-interactions.tldr: shapiq unifies algorithms, visualizations, and benchmarks for explaining individual and joint contributions with Shapley methods.

paragraphs: Diffusion methods have shown strong image-generation results, but previous language-modeling work reported a substantial gap behind autoregressive models. This paper revisits simple masked discrete diffusion and finds that its performance has been underestimated. The authors improve both the training recipe and the mathematical objective used to train these models.

Their simplified, Rao-Blackwellized objective takes the form of a mixture of familiar masked language-modeling losses. This connects diffusion training to predicting missing text while enabling additional performance improvements. The objective can train encoder-only models with efficient sampling methods, including samplers that generate arbitrary-length text in a semi-autoregressive manner.

Across language-modeling benchmarks, models trained with the proposed approach and modern engineering practices reach a new state of the art among diffusion models. Their perplexity approaches that of autoregressive models, which narrows the reported gap without claiming that it disappears. The results emphasize how much training design and objective simplification can improve a comparatively straightforward masked diffusion approach to language generation.
neurips-2024-simple-and-effective-masked.tldr: Improved training and a simplified masked-diffusion objective produce language models whose perplexity approaches autoregressive performance.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether learning an entire hypothesis class can be characterized by learning all of its finite projections. Its compactness result says that, across broad settings, the answer is exact: the full class has transductive sample complexity m if and only if every finite projection has that same sample complexity.

The authors prove this equivalence for realizable and agnostic learning under proper metric losses, and for continuous losses on compact spaces. The result therefore links a potentially unrestricted learning problem to its finite restrictions without changing the required sample complexity. The permitted loss functions are central to the scope of that exact statement.

For realizable learning with improper metric losses, exact equality can fail. Matching upper and lower bounds show that sample complexities can differ by a factor of two; larger agnostic gaps are conjectured, not proved. Using an existing connection between transductive and PAC sample complexities in the realizable case, the authors also transfer the results to an almost-exact compactness statement for PAC learning.
neurips-2024-transductive-learning-is-co.tldr: For broad classes of losses, transductive learnability has exactly the same sample complexity as learnability of every finite projection.

paragraphs: Models of protein evolution use substitution rate matrices to describe changes between amino acids. Estimating these matrices typically requires reconstructing evolutionary trees from large collections of aligned proteins, creating a computational bottleneck. This paper develops a near-linear-time method that estimates the matrices from multiple sequence alignments alone.

The method relies on FastCherries, a near-linear-time cherry reconstruction algorithm that can handle alignments with millions of sequences. Tests on simulated and real data demonstrate speed and accuracy for a classical protein-evolution model. The resulting scalability also supports SiteRM, a richer model that estimates a separate general rate matrix for each alignment position.

On clinical and deep mutational scanning variant-effect data in ProteinGym, SiteRM outperforms large protein language models despite treating sites independently. The authors attribute the advantage to their probabilistic treatment of evolutionary data and ability to use very large alignments. The finding shows that, in these evaluations, scalable evolutionary modeling can outperform models that learn more complex interactions between protein positions.
neurips-2024-ultrafast-classical-phyloge.tldr: Fast evolutionary-rate estimation enables SiteRM to outperform large protein language models on the reported ProteinGym variant-effect evaluations.
